title: Impact of Police Staffing on Crime Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV) / Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS)**

**Why:** The research question explicitly identifies an endogeneity problem: police staffing (x) and crime rates (y) are simultaneously determined. Higher crime may lead to more police hiring (reverse causality), and omitted variables (e.g., poverty, urbanization) may affect both. OLS estimates of the effect of police on crime would be biased.

**Instrument:** The cops grant lottery (z) provides exogenous variation in police staffing. Lottery assignment is random, making it an ideal instrument.

**Key assumptions:**
1. **Relevance:** The grant lottery (z) significantly affects police staffing (x). Testable via first-stage F-statistic.
2. **Exclusion restriction:** The lottery affects crime rates *only* through its effect on police staffing, not through any other channel. Plausible because lottery assignment is random.
3. **Independence:** The lottery is as-good-as-random (by design), so z is uncorrelated with unobserved determinants of crime.

We expect OLS to be biased upward (toward positive/less negative) because high-crime areas hire more police, while IV should reveal the true negative causal effect of police on crime.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# IV Analysis: Impact of Police Staffing on Crime Rates
# ============================================================

# Load required packages
if (!require("AER")) install.packages("AER", repos="https://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("lmtest")) install.packages("lmtest", repos="https://cran.r-project.org")
if (!require("sandwich")) install.packages("sandwich", repos="https://cran.r-project.org")

library(AER)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# --- Read Data ---
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s84_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Columns:", names(df), "\n\n")
summary(df)

# ============================================================
# 1. OLS Estimation (Naive / Benchmark)
# ============================================================
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("1. OLS ESTIMATION (Naive)\n")
cat("========================================\n")

ols_no_controls <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)
ols_with_controls <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)

cat("\n--- OLS without controls ---\n")
print(summary(ols_no_controls))

cat("\n--- OLS with controls ---\n")
print(summary(ols_with_controls))

# ============================================================
# 2. First Stage: z -> x
# ============================================================
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("2. FIRST STAGE: Grant Lottery -> Police Count\n")
cat("========================================\n")

first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
print(summary(first_stage))

# First-stage F-statistic on excluded instrument
first_stage_restricted <- lm(x ~ controls, data = df)
f_test <- anova(first_stage_restricted, first_stage)
cat("\n--- First-Stage F-test on excluded instrument ---\n")
print(f_test)
f_stat <- f_test$F[2]
cat(sprintf("\nFirst-stage F-statistic: %.2f\n", f_stat))
cat(sprintf("Rule of thumb: F > 10 indicates strong instrument. %s\n",
            ifelse(f_stat > 10, "PASSED", "WARNING: Weak instrument")))

# ============================================================
# 3. IV / 2SLS Estimation
# ============================================================
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("3. IV / 2SLS ESTIMATION\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# IV without controls
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
cat("\n--- IV without controls ---\n")
print(summary(iv_no_controls, diagnostics = TRUE))

# IV with controls
iv_with_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
cat("\n--- IV with controls ---\n")
print(summary(iv_with_controls, diagnostics = TRUE))

# Robust standard errors for IV
cat("\n--- IV with controls (Robust SEs) ---\n")
robust_iv <- coeftest(iv_with_controls, vcov = vcovHC(iv_with_controls, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_iv)

# ============================================================
# 4. Reduced Form: z -> y
# ============================================================
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("4. REDUCED FORM: Grant Lottery -> Crime Rate\n")
cat("========================================\n")

reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Manual Wald/IV estimate
rf_coef <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
fs_coef <- coef(first_stage)["z"]
wald_estimate <- rf_coef / fs_coef
cat(sprintf("\nWald (IV) estimate = Reduced Form / First Stage = %.4f / %.4f = %.4f\n",
            rf_coef, fs_coef, wald_estimate))

# ============================================================
# 5. Summary Comparison
# ============================================================
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("5. SUMMARY: OLS vs. IV COMPARISON\n")
cat("========================================\n")

ols_coef <- coef(ols_with_controls)["x"]
ols_se <- summary(ols_with_controls)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]
iv_coef <- coef(iv_with_controls)["x"]
iv_se <- summary(iv_with_controls)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]

cat(sprintf("OLS coefficient on police (x):  %.4f  (SE: %.4f)\n", ols_coef, ols_se))
cat(sprintf("IV  coefficient on police (x):  %.4f  (SE: %.4f)\n", iv_coef, iv_se))
cat(sprintf("First-stage F-statistic:        %.2f\n", f_stat))
cat(sprintf("\nDifference (IV - OLS):          %.4f\n", iv_coef - ols_coef))

cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
if (iv_coef < ols_coef) {
  cat("IV estimate is more negative than OLS, consistent with upward bias in OLS\n")
  cat("due to reverse causality (high-crime areas hire more police).\n")
} else {
  cat("IV estimate is less negative (or more positive) than OLS.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# 6. Robustness Checks
# ============================================================
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("6. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# 6a. Hausman test for endogeneity
cat("\n--- 6a. Hausman Test (OLS vs IV) ---\n")
# Manual Hausman: include first-stage residuals in OLS
df$fs_residuals <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_reg <- lm(y ~ x + controls + fs_residuals, data = df)
hausman_pval <- summary(hausman_reg)$coefficients["fs_residuals", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Coefficient on first-stage residuals: %.4f (p-value: %.4f)\n",
            coef(hausman_reg)["fs_residuals"], hausman_pval))
cat(sprintf("Endogeneity test: %s at 5%% level\n",
            ifelse(hausman_pval < 0.05, "REJECT exogeneity of x", "Cannot reject exogeneity")))

# 6b. Check balance: lottery should be uncorrelated with controls
cat("\n--- 6b. Balance Check: Lottery vs Controls ---\n")
balance_test <- lm(z ~ controls, data = df)
balance_pval <- summary(balance_test)$coefficients["controls", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Regression of z on controls: coef = %.4f, p-value = %.4f\n",
            coef(balance_test)["controls"], balance_pval))
cat(sprintf("Balance: %s\n",
            ifelse(balance_pval > 0.05, "PASSED (lottery uncorrelated with controls)",
                   "WARNING: Potential imbalance")))

# 6c. Anderson-Rubin confidence interval (robust to weak instruments)
cat("\n--- 6c. Anderson-Rubin Test (Weak-IV Robust) ---\n")
# Grid search for AR confidence set
beta_grid <- seq(-3, 3, by = 0.01)
ar_pvals <- sapply(beta_grid, function(b) {
  resid_test <- df$y - b * df$x
  ar_reg <- lm(resid_test ~ z + controls, data = df)
  f_val <- summary(ar_reg)$fstatistic
  if (is.null(f_val)) return(1)
  coef_summary <- summary(ar_reg)$coefficients
  if ("z" %in% rownames(coef_summary)) {
    return(coef_summary["z", "Pr(>|t|)"])
  }
  return(1)
})
ar_ci <- beta_grid[ar_pvals > 0.05]
if (length(ar_ci) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("Anderson-Rubin 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", min(ar_ci), max(ar_ci)))
} else {
  cat("Anderson-Rubin CI: Could not construct (all rejected)\n")
}

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("ANALYSIS COMPLETE\n")
cat("========================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign and magnitude:**

1. **OLS estimate:** Likely biased upward (toward zero or even positive). Because police are endogenously allocated to high-crime areas, the OLS coefficient may understate the crime-reducing effect of police or even show a spurious positive correlation (more police associated with more crime).

2. **IV estimate:** Expected to be **negative and larger in magnitude** than the OLS estimate, reflecting the true causal effect that more police reduce crime. Given the data scaling (standardized-looking variables), I'd expect a coefficient roughly in the range of **-0.3 to -0.8** — a meaningful deterrent effect.

3. **First stage:** The lottery instrument should have a **strong positive** effect on police staffing (F-stat well above 10), since winning the grant enables hiring.

4. **Reduced form:** The lottery should have a **negative** direct association with crime rates, confirming the causal chain (lottery → more police → less crime).

5. **Hausman test:** Likely to reject exogeneity of police staffing, confirming the need for IV.

6. **The gap between OLS and IV** illustrates the classic simultaneous equations bias in the police-crime literature (as in Levitt 1997), where naive correlations mask the true deterrent effect of policing.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use the cops grant lottery as an instrument for police count.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased police staffing significantly reduces crime rates.
